findings.reason: At head, renderer.ts:307-324 has no `code_inline` case, so those tokens fall through to `default: // all other tokens are skipped`. renderer.ts:108-109 builds the image alt from renderInlineAsText, and backticks.ts:42 pushes code_inline tokens, so `![foo `bar`](x)` now gets alt="foo " instead of "foo bar".
findings.claim: Removing the code_inline case from renderInlineAsText drops code-span text from image alt attributes, against the CommonMark stripped-markup rule.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `case 'code_inline':` and its comment `// code content is added as plain text, without backticks`. code_inline tokens now reach `default: // all other tokens are skipped` (line 322). The image rule at line 109 builds alt from `slf.renderInlineAsText(token.children!, ...)`, and backticks.ts:42 pushes `code_inline` tokens into those children.

findings.reason: Searching test/ for an image whose alt contains a backtick (`!\[[^\]]*`[^\]]*\]`) finds nothing, so no locked test covers the deleted branch and the regression would pass the gate. acceptance.md only points to story.md and tests.lock, and neither is in the packet. I lowered severity to low because this is a coverage gap behind C1/X1, not a separate defect.
findings.claim: No test locks image alt text containing inline code, so the alt-text regression can pass the acceptance gate unseen.
findings.evidence: acceptance.md only points to an absent story.md and tests.lock (no such files exist in the export or packet). A search of test/ for an image whose alt contains backticks (`!\[.*`.*`.*\]\(`) finds no matches, so no pass-to-pass test covers the deleted branch.
